hypotheses.title: Risk-Adjusted Intermediate Momentum
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Investors underreact to steady, consistent positive fundamental news drift, but overreact to lottery-like spikes. Scaling 20-day returns by historical realized return volatility isolates persistent drift and suppresses turnover.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha performance degrades when realized volatility spikes or after controlling for broad market momentum.

hypotheses.title: Lagged Risk-Adjusted Momentum
hypotheses.economic_rationale: 1-to-5 day price changes are frequently dominated by short-term microstructural reversal, order imbalance bounces, and liquidity provision. Delaying the 20-day Sharpe momentum calculation by 5 days isolates institutional accumulation while bypassing short-term bid-ask reversal.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Signal underperforms standard unlagged momentum during sudden momentum regime transitions.

candidates.rationale: 20-day Sharpe momentum lagged by 5 trading days to bypass short-term reversal

hypotheses.title: Quarterly High Proximity & Resistance Breakout
hypotheses.economic_rationale: George and Hwang (2004) showed that proximity to historical intermediate price highs drives continuation due to investor anchoring bias. As price trades near its 60-day maximum, resistance dissolves, anchoring disappears, and prices drift upward.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha demonstrates mean-reversion rather than continuation near quarterly highs across small-cap regimes.

candidates.rationale: Ratio of current closing price to 60-day maximum high price
